A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying feature-tokenized, cross-attention GNN framework, renamed from AMPNet to FIMP. Both contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices sufficient for comparison despite substantial reframing and experimental revisions.

before.justification: V2 reports original fMRI and gene-expression reconstruction, image reconstruction, link prediction, node classification, and attention case-study results.

after.justification: V3 retains original reconstruction, classification, and attention analyses and adds results for pretrained-model variants and restricted-data gene-expression experiments.

M1.justification: The base cross-attention equations and Algorithm 1 remain, but v3 Section 3.4 adds a substantive extension: adapting pretrained foundation-model attention weights into cross-node message-passing operators and finetuning them. BrainLM and scGPT supply pretrained operators, while GenePT supplies gene embeddings. This changes the proposed training procedure beyond renaming AMPNet.

E1.justification: The quantitative OGBN-arXiv link-prediction task in v2 Table 3 is removed. OGBN-arXiv remains in v3 Appendix A.6 for attention analysis, and the fMRI, spatial-genomics, image-reconstruction, and node-classification coverage remains. The reduced-cell and increased-masking experiments modify settings within the retained gene-expression task.

E2.justification: GIN is added to the fMRI and spatial-genomics comparisons. GPS is newly evaluated in the spatial-genomics table, having already appeared in the fMRI comparison in v2. V3 also includes FIMP + ViT as a pretraining control; the CIFAR-100 and node-classification comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the reported UK Biobank sample from 1,000 to 76,250 recordings while retaining the 80/10/10 split. V3 Section 4.3 introduces a gene-expression condition restricted to 1,000 cells with 80% masking, versus 20% masking in the full-data setting. These are substantial reported protocol changes, although the retained normalization reference to 'all 1000 recordings' leaves that preprocessing detail ambiguous.

E4.justification: V2's fMRI comparison with and without positional encoding is removed. V3 adds analyses comparing base and pretrained operators, GenePT/scGPT variants, full versus restricted gene-expression data, and an out-of-domain ViT control to examine transfer benefits. The three attention case studies remain unchanged in substance; the biological studies move into the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs for the fMRI and spatial-genomics benchmarks and state five training runs for node classification, retaining the same use of ± values. No new seed-reporting practice, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces fMRI scores under the revised reported cohort: the positional-encoding model's MSE changes from 0.410 to 0.288, with R2 remaining 0.578, and BrainLM adds MSE 0.267/R2 0.606. Table 2 adds baseline, pretrained, and restricted-data results while retaining existing full-data entries. OGBN-arXiv AUROC results, including AMPNet's 89.5 ± 0.13, disappear. CIFAR-100 and node-classification scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the feature-embedding map, and the mathematical content of the message-passing pseudocode are retained. V3's pretrained-weight adaptation is a procedural extension; it introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: V2 presents the central contribution as interpretable feature-level interactions and richer node representations. V3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion redefine the main contribution as transferring knowledge from nongraph foundation models into GNN message-passing operators. The headline performance claims are consequently framed as evidence for foundation-model transfer.

C2.justification: V3 adds the interpretation that pretrained knowledge particularly benefits scarce-data settings and attributes the advantage over ViT initialization to domain-matched pretraining. V2's explicit qualification that attention weights are not completely faithful explanations is removed, although the biological interpretations based on attention remain in the appendix. These change substantive mechanism explanations and qualifications.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies Adam, cosine annealing with five cycles, and PyTorch Geometric, and expands Tables 5–7 with GIN and spatial-task GPS hyperparameters. V2's OGBN-arXiv preprocessing instructions—lemmatization, stop-word removal, and selection of 100 words by TF-IDF variance—are removed despite retaining the attention case study. Most existing hyperparameters and hardware information remain.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion shifts from post-hoc GNN explanations and interpretable attention models to foundation models, graph pretraining, and LLM graph reasoning. Numerous explanation references are removed, while works including scGPT, BrainLM, GenePT, GPT4Graph, and NLGraph are added. The claimed distinction from prior research becomes reuse of pretrained nongraph weights as message operators.

P1.justification: Beyond the AMPNet-to-FIMP rename, the abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Method subsections are reorganized around tokenization and foundation-informed message passing, and the main-text biological interpretability section moves into Appendix A.4–A.5. This substantially changes the narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is completely redrawn as a foundation-model transfer pipeline. Table 2 gains full/limited-data blocks, Table 3 loses its link-prediction column, and the hyperparameter tables gain columns and are consolidated onto one page. Figures 3–4 move into the appendix; the actual graphics in Figures 2–5 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful evidence about transfer through base-versus-pretrained comparisons, restricted-data tests, and the mismatched ViT control. Additional optimizer and scheduler details also aid reproduction. This supports a limited net improvement, tempered by reduced benchmark and ablation coverage, removal of the attention-faithfulness qualification, and unclear UKB normalization and configurations for the new pretrained variants.
